title: Security Proof for the Variant Without Function b
summary: Function b simplifies the existing proof, and no attack is known without it beyond necessary bottom-layer tweak handling; whether the proof extends to this variant remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the inverse-free single-keyed tweakable enciphering scheme, determine whether the security proof can be extended to a variant that omits the function $b$ wherever possible while retaining $b$ for the necessary handling of the tweak in the bottom layer. The function $b$ simplifies the security proof, and no attack is known for the variant without $b$ apart from the necessary bottom-layer tweak handling; establishing such an extension remains unresolved.

scope.domain: Security proofs for inverse-free single-keyed tweakable enciphering schemes.
parameters: Function b: a proof-simplifying scheme component required for tweak handling in the bottom layer
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the existing security proof extends when function b is omitted everywhere except in bottom-layer tweak handling.

citations.label: An Inverse-Free Single-Keyed Tweakable Enciphering Scheme

progress.summary: The paper explicitly asks whether its proof extends to the variant without function b. It notes that b simplifies the proof and that no attack is known when b is otherwise omitted, while its bottom-layer use remains necessary.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., An Inverse-Free Single-Keyed Tweakable Enciphering Scheme
